newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS -- Fifty thousand people attended the candlelight vigil at Victoria Park to mourn David Chan, who died while protesting Japan's claim to the Diaoyu or Senkaku Islands.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Former Chief Justice Sir T.L. Yang said he would retire if he failed to become the future Hong Kong chief executive, rather than exchanging his votes with other candidates to gain some other important post.
-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS -- Businessman Peter Wu hinted he might announce his intention to stand for the post of Hong Kong chief executive today.

-- Research by the University of Hong Kong showed that most of the territory's young people prefered to be called Hong Kongers rather than Chinese, and their confidence toward the future was going down.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The Government was considering submitting the plan to build the Mass Transit Railway's Tseung Kwan O line to the future chief executive instead of the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group to avoid going through the complicated JLG procedures.

-- Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO -- Chinese vice-Premier Qian Qichen said the work to set up the first session of the Selection Committee was under way and that the process reflected the essence of "Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong".
-- American Chinese Yue-sai Kan donated 100,000 yuan to set up Beijing University Yue-sai Kan Education Fund. It would give awards to girls who came top in their studies.
-- Pro-Beijing HONG KONG COMMERCIAL DAILY -- Hong Kong's container shipping business was not likely to recover in the next two years.

-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Governor Chris Patten will announce hundreds of new initiatives in his last policy address to show his determination to continue effective government before sovereignty reverted to China.
-- Mainland power company Wuhan Yangluo Power Shareholding Co planned to invest US$1.2 billion on its expansion, which it expected would be financed by an overseas share listing.
-- Measures were being considered to encourage multi-national companies to establish their headquarters in Shanghai's Pudong area in the hope of soaking up a surplus of office space.
-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- The APEC Business Advisory Council made propsals that it said would cut the cost of financing infrastructure projects by 25 to 50 basis points.
